title: A complex with cohomology in a single degree is that cohomology object shifted
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category, $D(\mathcal C)$ its derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with cohomology functors $H^n$, and let $K\in D(\mathcal C)$ and $r\in\mathbf Z$ with $H^n(K)=0$ for every $n\neq r$. Then $K\cong A[-r]$ in $D(\mathcal C)$ for an object $A$ of $\mathcal C$ (the complex with $A$ in degree $r$), and necessarily $A\cong H^r(K)$.

source.place: Derived Categories, Remark Tag 08J5 (label remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle) applied twice: if $H^n(K)=0$ for $n\neq r$, the maps $\tau_{\leq r}K\to K$ and $\tau_{\leq r}K\to\tau_{\geq r}\tau_{\leq r}K$ are quasi-isomorphisms and the last complex is $H^r(K)$ placed in degree $r$

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: the hypotheses `X.IsGE r`, `X.IsLE r` are the vanishing of $H^n$ for $n<r$ and $n>r$ by `DerivedCategory.isGE_iff`, `isLE_iff`; $A\cong H^r(K)$ by applying `homologyFunctor C r` to the isomorphism
